decisionsTitle: The outbox paces Mailgun to an hourly allowance, and a rate refusal is a pause, never a loss (amending §100 and §163)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-01, forwarding Mailgun's notice:** «Urgent! Am primit asta de la Mailgun!» The notice put the club's account on Mailgun's probation: a new account, or one just moved to a paid plan, may send at most **100 messages an hour per domain**, and past that the account is temporarily disabled. (The notice's own text was not relayed to the branch; this paraphrases what it says.)

**The day.** The club took a paid plan and opened registrations the same morning: the morning a race's confirmations, declaration requests and the club's copies all leave at once, against an account that had just become a "new" one again.

**What the code did.** Nothing paced Mailgun: the outbox sent as fast as the queue filled — twenty a batch from the job, twenty from every request's drain under «imediat», forty from every «Trimite acum». A **429** was a transient failure (§40: "the hourly rate limit, which clears within the hour"), so it got the ordinary backoff — one, two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty-two minutes — and after the sixth attempt, about an hour, the message was **FAILED**: a runner's confirmation lost, and the account knocked on six more times while Mailgun was asking it to stop. A **400** "Domain … is not allowed to send: … temporarily disabled" matched no limit language (`ALLOWANCE_SPENT`, §40), so it was **permanent** — BOUNCED, never tried again. Nothing in the plan setting (§100) knew an hourly figure existed.

**Decision — A, the pace.** The email plan setting gains `hourlyAllowance` (1–100 000, or empty), **100 when the stored value has none**, so production paces from the first deploy without anybody touching it. An Administrator sets it on «Setări» → «Emailuri» → «Limita pe oră», with one line of help and the probation behind its «?», in both languages; the audit row `email_plan.changed` names it from and to, like the plan's ceilings. Before claiming Mailgun's road, `claimOutboxBatch` counts in one query what Mailgun carried in the trailing sixty minutes (`sent_at` inside the window, every road but Gmail's, captured messages excluded — they never reached Mailgun) and what another worker holds for it right now, and claims at most `hourlyAllowance − that`, oldest first. What is not claimed is not touched: no `next_attempt_at` is written, and the next drain or job run (every fifteen minutes by day) takes it when the hour has room. Gmail's road is not held to it. The after-response drain and «Trimite acum» go through the same claim; a press the hour has no room for is refused with its own sentence (`SEND_NOW_HOUR_SPENT`: «Alege «Pune la coadă»; emailul pleacă singur când ora are din nou loc.»), exactly as the day's allowance refuses (§80, §540). `/admin/emails` says «Trimise în ultima oră: N din 100» beside the day's count. `/api/health` counts rows held for the hour as `hourPaced`, not `overdue`, while a pace is set and Mailgun carried a message in the last ninety minutes — the same judgement the queue panel's red «late» makes (§529).

**Decision — B, the refusals.** `classifyMailgunFailure(status, body, headers)` — the adapter now hands it the response's headers. A **429** is a **pause**: throttled, `paced`, due again at Mailgun's `Retry-After` (seconds or an HTTP date; never in the past, never more than a day), or in fifteen minutes without one. A **400** whose body says "not allowed to send" *together with* disabled, probation, too fast, rate limit or temporarily is the same pause, fifteen minutes. The outbox gives the attempt back on a pause — a pause is not a refusal of the message, so no number of pauses spends the six attempts — keeps the reason on the row, and holds the rest of the batch's Mailgun messages until the same instant instead of knocking again at once. A message Mailgun keeps pausing past the overdue allowance since it was queued is `overdue` on `/api/health`, pace or no pace: a pause that never ends needs a person, and `lastError` says which refusal.

**Why 100 by default.** The probation is in force now. A pace that is too low costs minutes — the queue leaves a little later, and nothing is lost; one that is too high costs the account, disabled on registration morning. Once Mailgun's support lifts the probation, the Administrator raises the figure or clears it (`SETUP.md` §35).

**Kept.** Nothing is lost: an unclaimed row waits untouched, a paused one waits with its attempt. The daily deferral is unchanged — 402, 420 and a 400 with limit language still go to the reset (§40, §100). The 400s §40 keeps permanent stay permanent: the sandbox's «Sandbox subdomains are for test purposes only» and its unauthorized recipient, an unverified domain, a malformed message; 401 and 403 stay permanent. Gmail's road, its cap and its pace are unaffected (§443). The plan catalogue is unchanged: no plan row carries an hourly figure.

**What it does not cover.** Each environment counts only its own outbox, and QA sends through the same domain (§307): a QA rehearsal's messages come off production's hour at Mailgun without production knowing. `SETUP.md` §35 says to keep rehearsals small during the probation, or set QA's box lower. A Gmail-road message that falls back to Mailgun after a Gmail failure is not counted before it leaves; if it tips the hour over, Mailgun's 429 pauses it.

**Tests.** Unit `notifications/mailgun-classification.test.ts`: a 429 with `Retry-After: 847`, with an HTTP date, without one, with an unreadable or absurd one; the probation's 400 paused; the sandbox's 400 with "not allowed to send" still permanent; every earlier case unchanged. Unit `notifications/mailgun-adapter.test.ts`: the response's `Retry-After` reaches the classifier. Unit `notifications/email-plan.test.ts`: the default of 100 from an old value, a cleared box, the bounds, no catalogue row with an hourly figure, the room arithmetic. Integration `notifications/hourly-pace.test.ts` (PGlite): 100 sent in the last hour → no Mailgun row claimed and Gmail's as before; 60 → 40, oldest first, Gmail's sends not counted; 100 sent 61 minutes ago → a full batch; another worker's batch counted; a pause hands the batch back with its attempts and is not claimed early; twelve pauses never FAIL a message; «Trimite acum» and a resend's «now» refused with the hour's sentence; health's `hourPaced` and the paused row that turns overdue; the setting's default, round trip and audit row; the page's figure.

**Amends** §100 (the setting gains a field that is not a plan's), §40 (a 429 was transient, a "not allowed to send" 400 without limit language permanent) and §163 (a QA that may address anyone, through the club's domain since §307, now also spends the domain's hour).

*Rejected:* slowing the job's cadence — the after-response drain and «Trimite acum» would still burst a hundred in a minute; a cap in the Mailgun plan catalogue — the probation is the account's, not the plan's, and it ends when support lifts it; treating every 400 as a pause — a bad address, the sandbox's refusal or an unverified domain must stay permanent, or the outbox retries a hopeless message forever.
changelogLine: - **Mailgun's hourly limit is respected** — the outbox sends at most the hour's allowance (100 by default, set on «Emailuri») and pauses on a rate refusal instead of giving up, so a new account on probation never gets disabled and no confirmation email is lost. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given the email plan's «Limita pe oră» (100 when never set; empty is no pace), when the outbox claims a batch — the job, the drain after a response or «Trimite acum» — then Mailgun's road takes at most the allowance less what Mailgun carried in the trailing sixty minutes and what another worker holds, oldest first; Gmail's road is not held to it; an unclaimed row keeps its turn and attempts; a «now» press the hour has no room for is refused with its own sentence; `/admin/emails` shows «Trimise în ultima oră: N din …»; and `/api/health` counts rows held for the hour as `hourPaced`, not overdue, while Mailgun carried a message in the last ninety minutes (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given Mailgun answers a send with a 429, or a 400 saying it is not allowed to send because the account is disabled, on probation, too fast, rate limited or temporarily stopped, when the outbox records it, then the message is PENDING again at Mailgun's `Retry-After` (seconds or an HTTP date) or fifteen minutes later, its attempt given back so no number of pauses marks it FAILED, the batch's other Mailgun rows wait with it, and once it has waited past the overdue allowance since it was queued `/api/health` counts it overdue; the sandbox's and an unverified domain's 400s, 401 and 403 stay permanent, and the daily allowance's refusals still wait for the reset (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the outbox paces Mailgun to 100 an hour; a rate refusal is a pause
